## Basic two part conditional `if_else()`

Flag attendances that were above 20,000

using **if** _this_, do _this_ **else** do _that_

```{r}
data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data |>
  dplyr::mutate(above_20000 = dplyr::if_else(attendances >= 20000, "Y", "N"))
```

## Watch out for data types!

:::{.callout-note collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
Data types and outputs for two conditions need to be the same
:::

This breaks:

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::mutate(above_20000 = dplyr::if_else(attendances >= 20000, 100, "9999"))
```

## More than one conditional

::: {.incremental}
- `if_else` is great for a single conditional
- you can nest `if_else` statements but that gets really messy quickly
- especially with all the brackets!
- A multi part conditional to use would be a case statement.
:::


## Using `case_when()`

Let's create a grouping column for our attendances in 5000s

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ "Less than 5,000",
      attendances < 10000 ~ "5,000 to 9,999",
      attendances < 15000 ~ "10,000 to 14,999",
      attendances < 20000 ~ "15,000 to 19,999",
      attendances < 25000 ~ "20,000 to 24,999",
      .default = "Over 25,0000"
    )
  )
```

## What are `.default` and `~`?

::: {.incremental}
- `.default` argument is the same as 'else' 
- the `~` is the 'then'
:::

In case you see old code as this will still run

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "9"
data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ "Less than 5,000",
      attendances < 10000 ~ "5,000 to 9,999",
      attendances < 15000 ~ "10,000 to 14,999",
      attendances < 20000 ~ "15,000 to 19,999",
      attendances < 25000 ~ "20,000 to 24,999",
      TRUE ~ "Over 25,0000"
    )
  )
```

`TRUE` is the 'else' statement and you use `~` rather than `=`

## Making mistakes

::: {.incremental}
- This case statement fails if we have a value of **exactly** 25,000
- well not fail, just puts something in the wrong category
:::

```{r}
data_to_show_problems <- data

# change the first row to 25000
data_to_show_problems$attendances[1] <- 25000

data$attendances[1]
data_to_show_problems$attendances[1]
```

## Default is "over 25k" when it is 25k

```{r}
data_to_show_problems <- data_to_show_problems |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ "Less than 5,000",
      attendances < 10000 ~ "5,000 to 9,999",
      attendances < 15000 ~ "10,000 to 14,999",
      attendances < 20000 ~ "15,000 to 19,999",
      attendances < 25000 ~ "20,000 to 24,999",
      .default = "Over 25,0000"
    )
  )

data_to_show_problems
```

## Adding nulls

```{r}
data_to_show_problems$attendances[2] <- NA

data_to_show_problems

data_to_show_problems |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ "Less than 5,000",
      attendances < 10000 ~ "5,000 to 9,999",
      attendances < 15000 ~ "10,000 to 14,999",
      attendances < 20000 ~ "15,000 to 19,999",
      attendances < 25000 ~ "20,000 to 24,999",
      .default = "Over 25,0000"
    )
  )
```

## Better use of `.default` as a "catch"

Use the true statement as an error catch

```{r}
data_to_show_problems |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_grouping = dplyr::case_when(
      attendances < 5000 ~ "Less than 5,000",
      attendances < 10000 ~ "5,000 to 9,999",
      attendances < 15000 ~ "10,000 to 14,999",
      attendances < 20000 ~ "15,000 to 19,999",
      attendances < 25000 ~ "20,000 to 24,999",
      attendances > 25000 ~ "Over 25,0000",
      .default = "ERROR - does not compute"
    )
  )
```

## Over to you

Add a column to determine:

- **if** type `1` **then** half the attendances
- **if** type `2` **then** triple the attendances
- **if** type `other` **then** quadruple the attendances
- **if** errors **then** a suitable error message

:::{.callout-tip collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
Remember the data types need to be the same
:::

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 10,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - fixing the `.default` and 'ERROR - does not compute'


```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    attendance_multliper = dplyr::case_when(
      type == "1" ~ attendances * 0.5,
      type == "2" ~ attendances * 3,
      type == "other" ~ attendances * 4,
      .default = -9999
    )
  )
```
